chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Al-Khattab ibn Salama, from Hisham ibn Ahmad, who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon his master's death) who killed a man by error. He (peace be upon him) said: 'What have you been narrated regarding this?' I said: 'We have been narrated from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: He is handed over in full to the guardians of the slain. So when the one who promised his freedom (upon his own death) dies, he is freed.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Glory be to Allah! So the blood of a Muslim man is invalidated?' I said: 'This is how we have been narrated.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'You have erred regarding my father. He is handed over in full to the guardians of the slain. So when the one who promised his freedom dies, he is asked to pay his value.'

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءِ الْمَقْتُولِ: Guardians of the slain: The heirs entitled to blood money or compensation
key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ فِي قِيمَتِهِ: He is asked to pay his value: The requirement to compensate the heirs for the slave's worth to gain freedom
key_terms.مُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave manumitted upon the death of his master

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a Mudabbir who kills a man accidentally?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Kulayni records Imam al-Rida (AS) correcting a prevalent narration regarding a *Mudabbir* who commits accidental homicide, emphasizing that the slave does not automatically gain freedom upon his master's death but must instead pay the value of his remaining servitude to the victim's heirs. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that the *Mudabbir* retains a distinct legal status where his manumission is conditional upon settling the financial liability (*diyah* of his slavery) rather than being a direct consequence of the master's demise. The Imam’s correction underscores the precision required in deriving legal rulings from transmitted reports, ensuring that the rights of the victim's heirs are preserved through monetary compensation rather than automatic emancipation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail Bin Marrar, from Yunus, from Al Khattab Bin Salama, from Hisham Bin Ahmad who said,

‘I asked Abu Al-Hassanasws about a Mudabbir (slave promised freedom upon the death of his master), who killed a man in error. Heasws said: ‘Which thing are you all reporting with regards to this?’ I said, ‘We are reporting from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘He would be completely handed over to the guardians of the killed one. So when the one who promised his freedom upon his own death were to die, he is free’. Heasws said: ‘Glory be to Allahazwj! So the blood of a Muslim person has been invalidated?’ I said, ‘This is how we are reporting it’. Heasws said: ‘You are mistaken upon myasws fatherasws. He would be completely handed over to the guardians of the killed one. So when the one who promised him freedom upon his own death were to die, he has to work with regards to his value’.
